title: After the rain
commonName: Paintable wet material and clearcoat shader
description: Water brushed across deep green stone accumulates into a glossy region, revealing a sharp grazing reflection beside the same dry material.
useCase: Show the difference between matte and coated finishes in a tactile material selector or product story.
interaction: Drag to wet the stone. Arrow keys place the brush and Space or Enter paints; Dry surface clears it.
reducedMotion: Direct painting remains available. Automatic drying freezes under reduced motion; Dry surface is an immediate deterministic reset.
limitations: A procedural stone sample, screen-space brush mask and authored strip-light response, not a physically calibrated BRDF or fluid simulation. The bounded mask dries while active and visible. Requires WebGL 1; interaction disables with an explicit fallback and resumes after context restoration.
look: A large beveled mineral-green stone sample seen straight from above on dark green, thin light veins and subdued dark fractures; a brushed wet region catches a crisp white reflection with an irregular absorbent edge.
motion: A persistent canvas mask records contiguous brush strokes. Wetness changes diffuse tint and a separate clearcoat highlight; wet roughness changes the highlight width. Drying fades the mask only while active and visible.
adapt: `DEFAULT_CONFIG` and the `config` prop expose brush radius, dry and wet roughness, and drying time. `relief` defines the original stone field. `paint` updates the persistent `mask`; `step` advances drying, while `useSurface` uploads it as a texture and stops rendering when dry or paused.
